known_answer_check.arm_expects: summarizer draws on every turn plus one episodic draw per session boundary

cost.note: serving and summarizer are SEPARATE model ids and separate quota windows (G-P11); they are never summed into one row without the split.

metrics.corpus_label: Derived from a harness-authored synthetic session corpus (P4, R91). Its resemblance to real usage is unproven and was not tested: no real traffic exists to compare against (D3), and the corpus was declared unvalidated by choice rather than validated by a check. Its composition is a pre-registered design parameter -- 40 sessions across five families, 50% literal-bearing -- chosen for measurability, not realism, and its cache repeat rate is a dial, not an observation. Per-family figures are reported separately so any reweighting is arithmetic rather than a regeneration.

a.name: task success on scripted multi-turn goals
a.gold_required: Per-turn authored gold, 108 rows: for each turn, the goal it advances and a machine-checkable success predicate (an expected entity, chapter, or refusal). The corpus has none -- every turn is {query}. A9 makes this a NEW VERSION STAMP of test/session_corpus.json (a re-freeze with its own pre-registration, CP-4a shape), not an added field: src/harness/sessions.py refuses a modified file. Cost rider (R120): authored gold on a corpus already declared unvalidated (R91/O5) compounds the O5/O10 label rather than fixing it.

b.name: answer quality at turn N given information introduced at turn 1
b.gold_required: Either (i) per-session authored gold stating what a turn-N answer must retain from turn 1 -- 68 follow-up turns, again a corpus re-freeze under A9 -- or (ii) a judge. The judge exists (scripts/eval_quality.py, Config.JUDGE_MODEL) but is METERED, so it cannot run on Batch B's $0 fake arm; A7 pins it to Tier 2 (reports, never gates) and R63 records that it cannot arbitrate quality here. A further blocker specific to this batch: the fake provider replays one fixed fixture, so on the fake arm every arm's answer text is identical by construction and there is nothing for a judge to score.

c.name: retrieval-style recall over what should have been in context
c.gold_required: Already present: session-level `targets`, one {book, part, chapter} per session, on 35 of 40 sessions (95 of 108 turns). Constant within a session, so per-turn scoring is possible but turn-to-turn discrimination is not (R120 qualifier 2).

overall.note: arithmetic only -- decisions are taken per family (R91/R119), never on this row

passages.value_reason: scored from the context plan alone, which is the allocator's own output; CP-6b refuses that as a metric. An external signal for this tier's value does not exist in the frozen corpus -- see FAMILIES['a'] and ['b'] for the gold it would take.

recent_turns.value_reason: scored from the context plan alone, which is the allocator's own output; CP-6b refuses that as a metric. An external signal for this tier's value does not exist in the frozen corpus -- see FAMILIES['a'] and ['b'] for the gold it would take.

episodic.value_reason: scored from the context plan alone, which is the allocator's own output; CP-6b refuses that as a metric. An external signal for this tier's value does not exist in the frozen corpus -- see FAMILIES['a'] and ['b'] for the gold it would take.

tier_value.note: allocation, not value. A cache-hit or retrieval-only turn composes no prompt and emits no context_plan; those are counted, not treated as an empty allocation.
